issues.legal_issue: Municipal property tax and urban immoveable property tax imposed as recurring annual liabilities secured on property are deductible in computing income from that property as annual charges that are not capital charges.
material_facts: The assessee derived income from property and claimed deductions for municipal property tax and urban immoveable property tax paid during the relevant year.
The taxes were levied annually on the annual value of the property, with the annual liability payable in half-yearly instalments.
The governing enactments made the property a statutory security for payment of the taxes.
The High Court answered against deduction, and the assessee appealed.
issues.conclusion: Both taxes qualify as annual charges that are not capital charges, and their amounts are deductible in computing income from property under section 9(1)(iv) of the Indian Income-tax Act.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 9(1)(iv) of the Indian Income-tax Act, an annual charge means a charge securing an annual liability, while a capital charge means a charge securing a liability of a capital nature. A recurring annual liability does not cease to be annual because it is payable in instalments or varies in amount. The Court relied on Commissioner of Income-tax, Bombay v. Mahomedbhoy Rowji for the meaning of annual charge, while rejecting its conclusion on deductibility; it approved Gappumal Kanhaiya Lal v. Commissioner of Income-tax. It also relied on Moss Empires Ltd. v. Inland Revenue Commissioners and Cunard’s Trustees v. Inland Revenue Commissioners for the principle that variability or contingency does not prevent a payment from being annual. The statutory provisions creating the municipal tax and its property charge were sections 143, 146, 154, 156, 167, 197 and 212 of the City of Bombay Municipal Act, 1888; the urban tax and its property security arose under sections 22 and 24(2)(b) of the Bombay Finance Act, 1932. Bijoy Singh Dudhuria v. Commissioner of Income-tax was discussed as background to the amendment adding the annual-charge deduction. The separate allowance for land revenue under section 9(1)(v) did not exclude taxes that otherwise fell within section 9(1)(iv).

rule.if: property_income_tax_computation and tax_is_an_annual_property_levy and property_secures_payment_of_tax and not tax_secures_a_capital_liability

predicates.property_income_tax_computation: The assessment concerns income derived from property and the computation of that income for tax purposes.
predicates.tax_is_an_annual_property_levy: The tax is imposed recurrently on the annual value of the property, even if payable in instalments.
predicates.property_secures_payment_of_tax: The law makes the property security for payment of the tax.
predicates.tax_secures_a_capital_liability: The tax charge secures discharge of a liability of a capital nature.
predicates.annual_property_tax_is_deductible: The annual property tax is deductible in computing income from the property.

issues.definition: When property income is being computed, a recurring annual property tax secured on the property is deductible if the charge does not secure a liability of a capital nature.
